advisory.finding: `_refuse_unpublishable_store` runs the full ~5-call git subprocess divergence probe on EVERY event via `finalize_event`, which the transactional cores (txn.py, delete.py, inbound_translate.py) invoke multiple times per committed transaction under one lock — so a single multi-event write (e.g. STATUS+EDIT with an assignee) re-runs the identical local-only probe redundantly, adding per-event git-spawn latency to the hot write path.
merged_from: `finalize_event` now calls `_refuse_unpublishable_store` -> `write_blocking_divergence`, which spawns 3-4 git subprocesses, on EVERY event. In the delete-cascade path (`scan_and_write_unlinks`) `finalize_event` is invoked once per UNLINK inside a loop over the whole store / per-dep, so the divergence probe is re-run (with fresh subprocess fanout) O(N) times for a single delete, where N scales with store size and cross-link count. The probe result is invariant for the tracker within one command, so this is redundant per-event recomputation (N+1 subprocess calls in a loop).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish merge-base exit 1 (no common ancestor) from exit 128 (git error) before treating a non-zero return as proven divergence.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:253-258: `no_common_ancestor = ( run_git(tracker, "merge-base", "HEAD", remote_ref, check=False, ...).returncode != 0 )`
merge-base returns 1 for 'no merge base found' but 128 for a bad/unresolvable revision (e.g. unborn HEAD), so returncode!=0 conflates git error with proven divergence

freshness.py:259-261 documents fail-open intent: 'write publishability probe failed; allowing write' — but a git-level merge-base error escapes that path because it is a non-zero returncode, not an exception
advisory.finding: `write_blocking_divergence` treats any non-zero return from `merge-base HEAD remote_ref` as proof of no common ancestor, but git merge-base exits 128 (not 1) on an error such as an unresolvable/unborn HEAD; an empty or freshly-initialized tracker whose remote_ref exists and carries .store-compat.json would then be classified as a proven divergence and REFUSED, contradicting the module's documented fail-OPEN posture for probe errors.
advisory.suggested_fix: Only treat returncode == 1 as no-common-ancestor; treat other non-zero codes as probe failure and return None (allow).

test_fsck_reports_diverged_on_non_fast_forward (test_fsck_push_pending.py:137-176) asserts only fsck._tracker_sync_status classifier output — it never calls write_blocking_divergence nor performs a write, so it does not pin that a common-ancestor divergent store still permits writes.

Named violating input: a tracker with a shared base plus divergent local+remote commits (common ancestor exists) — write_blocking_divergence must return None so the write proceeds; no test asserts this.
advisory.finding: No test asserts that a common-ancestor (non-fast-forward / PUSH_PENDING) divergence is ALLOWED through the write path — the central narrow-contract boundary the diff introduces. The added guard `if not no_common_ancestor: return None` (freshness.py:262) distinguishes the refuse-worthy no-common-ancestor split from ordinary recoverable divergence, but every new test exercises only the no-common-ancestor refusal or remote/ref-mismatch None cases. A regression broadening the refusal to any divergence would go undetected.
scenarios: A future change tightens write_blocking_divergence to block any divergence (dropping the merge-base gate), converting a recoverable PUSH_PENDING store into a write outage — no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case reusing the setup from test_fsck_reports_diverged_on_non_fast_forward (common ancestor exists, neither side ancestor of the other) and assert `freshness.write_blocking_divergence(str(tracker)) is None`, plus that rebar.comment(seed, ...) succeeds and commits.

advisory.finding: No regression test proves the narrow refusal does NOT over-refuse an ordinary PUSH_PENDING / common-ancestor write routed through finalize_event. The design's load-bearing property is narrowness (only no-common-ancestor is refused; local-ahead and common-ancestor divergence must still write), yet only the refusal path is tested. A regression weakening `if not no_common_ancestor: return None` (line 265-266) would silently convert the store into a write outage.
